data.title: Stock Picks: Mega First And Ranhill Utilities
data.description:
RHB Research has identified Mega First Corporation Bhd and Ranhill Utilities Bhd as technical stock picks, citing bullish breakouts that could pave the way for further gains.

For Mega First, RHB Research said the counter’s uptrend could extend after it breached the RM2.90 resistance level, with Friday’s positive price action and close above the level indicating that bullish momentum is gaining pace.

Following the breakout, the research house expects the stock to move towards the next resistance levels at RM3.10 and RM3.20.

However, RHB Research cautioned that a breach of the RM2.80 support would be viewed as a bearish breakout and could open the door to further downside.

Meanwhile, Ranhill Utilities could see its uptrend continue after breaking above the RM2.60 resistance on strong trading volume.

RHB Research said the counter printed a fresh bullish candlestick after climbing above the resistance level last Friday, signalling that a bullish bias has emerged.

The research house expects Ranhill Utilities to move towards RM2.75, followed by RM2.90 if the bullish momentum persists.

A breach of the RM2.45 support, however, would be considered a bearish breakout and could lead to further downward movement.

data.title: Singapore Dollar Set For Further Upside Against USD
data.description:
The Singapore dollar strengthened against the US dollar following a sharp reversal in the greenback and a decline in long-term US Treasury yields, with OCBC Global Markets Research seeing scope for USD/SGD to move lower if broader US dollar weakness persists.

OCBC said USD/SGD declined after the US Treasury announced an expansion of its long-end bond buyback programme, helping drive long-dated Treasury yields lower.

The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell around 0.8%, which OCBC described as a relatively sizeable one-day move. Given the significant correlation between the DXY and USD/SGD, the research house said the impact of the broader dollar decline on the currency pair should not be understated.

While Singapore’s supportive economic fundamentals and the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER) policy framework remain important anchors for the currency, OCBC said the latest movement demonstrates that the direction of the US dollar remains a significant cyclical driver of USD/SGD.

The research house also noted that speculative positioning could leave the greenback vulnerable to further corrections.

According to OCBC, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data showed net-long positioning in the DXY was stretched by historical standards, potentially creating room for further US dollar weakness if additional downside surprises emerge.

“If USD weakness extends, there may be room for USD/SGD to drift lower even in the absence of a Singapore-specific driver,” OCBC said.

Separately, OCBC highlighted Singapore’s latest measures aimed at attracting and retaining hedge funds and senior investment professionals as supportive of the city-state’s longer-term position as an international financial centre.

These initiatives include tax incentives, a new hedge fund investment programme and a dedicated investment-management track under the existing Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) framework.

OCBC said the measures add to Singapore’s constructive medium-term financial-hub story, although their direct impact on Singapore dollar flows is likely to remain limited for now.

From a technical perspective, USD/SGD was last seen around 1.2720, with mild bearish momentum on the daily chart remaining intact.

OCBC cautioned, however, that the Relative Strength Index was approaching oversold territory, suggesting some possibility of two-way movement even as the broader bias remains lower.

The research house sees support at 1.2680, corresponding to the 76.4% Fibonacci retracement level.

Resistance is seen at 1.2740, followed by 1.2790 and the 1.2830-1.2840 region, which incorporates the 100-day and 200-day moving averages as well as a key Fibonacci retracement level.

Overall, OCBC expects downside pressure on USD/SGD to persist with the trading range increasingly skewed lower, particularly if the pullback in the US dollar and long-term Treasury yields continues.

data.title: Softer US Dollar Offers Relief For IDR
data.description:
The Indonesian rupiah could find some near-term relief from a softer US dollar and easing long-term US Treasury yields, according to OCBC Global Markets Research.

In its latest foreign exchange outlook, OCBC said Bank Indonesia’s decision to keep its policy rate unchanged at 5.75% reinforces policy continuity under acting Governor Destry Damayanti, with the central bank maintaining its focus on rupiah stability.

Bank Indonesia also reiterated measures aimed at attracting foreign capital inflows and deepening the country’s foreign exchange markets.

OCBC said the central bank appears increasingly inclined to rely on non-interest-rate measures, including foreign exchange hedging incentives and Bank Indonesia Rupiah Securities (SRBI), rather than raising domestic interest rates materially.

“A sustained USD pullback would ease some external pressure on IDR, although elevated oil prices remain a constraint for Indonesia,” the research house said.

The USD/IDR last closed around 17,830, with bearish momentum on the daily chart remaining intact while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) was broadly flat.

OCBC expects two-way trading in the near term, identifying support at 17,760 and 16,630, with the latter levels linked to technical indicators including the 100-day moving average and Fibonacci retracement. Resistance is seen at 17,940.

data.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum End Choppy Week Higher As Fed Bets Drive Crypto Swings
data.description:
Cryptocurrency markets ended the Aug 31-Sept 4 period modestly higher after a volatile week dominated by shifting US interest-rate expectations, Middle East tensions and institutional fund flows.

Based on Investing.com’s daily reference prices, Bitcoin rose about 2.7% from US$78,570 on Aug 31 to around US$80,713 on Sept 4, while Ethereum gained roughly 2.3% from US$2,468 to US$2,524 over the same period.

The week started on firmer footing as institutional demand provided support. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) also attracted about US$217 million of inflows at the start of the week, while Ether ETFs recorded an 11th consecutive session of net buying, helping underpin sentiment.

Momentum reversed on Sept 1 and Sept 2 as renewed US-Iran tensions sent oil prices and global bond yields sharply higher. Rising energy costs fuelled inflation concerns and pushed expectations for a September Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike towards 70%, prompting investors to trim exposure to risk assets. Bitcoin fell towards US$77,000, while Ethereum also came under pressure.

The strongest rebound came on Sept 3 after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled that he could support keeping rates unchanged if inflation continued to moderate, and this resulted to Bitcoin surging more than 5% to briefly top US$82,000, while Ethereum jumped nearly 5%, with short-covering adding momentum to the rally.

Gains were, however, pared on Sept 4 after the US economy added a stronger-than-expected 162,000 jobs in August, reviving bets that the Fed could raise rates this month. As such, Bitcoin slipped back below US$80,000 during the session as rate-hike expectations climbed to around 60%.

Overall, the week highlighted crypto’s continued sensitivity to Fed policy expectations, Treasury yields and geopolitical-driven oil prices, with institutional ETF demand providing a counterweight to macroeconomic uncertainty.

data.title: Hang Seng Ends Week Higher Despite Mid-Week Volatility
data.description:
Hong Kong equities ended the week higher, with the Hang Seng Index (HSI) gaining 83.88 points, or 0.33%, from 25,566.99 on 31 August to 25,650.87 on 4 September.

The HSI started the week slightly lower on Monday before falling 0.93% on Tuesday as investors remained cautious over US interest-rate expectations and rising Treasury yields.

The index remained under pressure through the middle of the week before staging a sharp rebound on Friday, gaining 437.56 points, or 1.74%, to close at 25,650.87.

The Hang Seng Tech Index rose 2.27% to 4,569.80 points on Friday, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index climbed 2.02% to 8,555.03 points, as technology and mainland-related counters led the recovery.

The week’s volatility came as investors weighed US monetary-policy expectations, economic data and regional growth signals. Higher Treasury yields and concerns over potential US rate hikes weighed on sentiment earlier in the week.

However, Friday’s strong rebound pointed to improved risk appetite towards Chinese equities and technology stocks, helping the HSI erase much of its earlier losses.

data.title: Kospi Ends Volatile Week 1.5% Lower As Iran Tensions Offset Export Boost
data.description:
South Korean stocks ended a turbulent week lower on Sept 4, as a sharp midweek sell-off triggered by escalating US-Iran tensions outweighed gains fuelled by strong exports and easing concerns over US interest rate hikes.

The benchmark Kospi finished at 6,687.21 on Sept 4, down about 1.5% for the week from 6,788.88 on Aug 28. The index gained 0.46% on Aug 31 and another 0.23% the following day before plunging 3.99% on Sept 2, its steepest move of the week. It recovered 0.26% the next day and surged 1.64% on Sept 4.

Chip heavyweights spearheaded the rebound on Sept 4, with Samsung Electronics climbing 2.2% and SK hynix advancing 3.2%, helping the Kospi claw back part of its midweek losses.

However, the rout on Sept 2 proved decisive after renewed US-Iran military clashes pushed crude prices higher, reviving inflation concerns and expectations that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) could tighten monetary policy further. Foreign and institutional investors dumped a combined 3.9 trillion won worth of shares that day, with Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Hyundai Motor and battery stocks suffering heavy losses.

Sentiment stabilised later in the week as oil-price pressures eased and Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled that rates could remain unchanged in September if disinflation continued, encouraging foreign and institutional investors to return to Korean equities.

Domestic economic data also provided support. South Korea’s exports jumped 68.7% year-on-year in August to US$98.26 billion, powered by booming demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related technology and semiconductors.

Further optimism came from Bank of Korea data showing a US$42.08 billion current account surplus in July, the second largest on record and the country’s 39th consecutive monthly surplus, driven largely by strong semiconductor exports.

Overall, the week highlighted a tug-of-war between South Korea’s powerful AI and semiconductor export cycle and external risks from Middle East tensions, oil prices and the Fed’s next rate move.

data.title: STI Climbs 46.60 Points In First Week Of September
data.description:
Singapore equities ended the week higher, with the Straits Times Index (STI) gaining 46.60 points, or 0.81%, from 5,755.36 on 31 August to 5,801.96 on 4 September.

The index started the week strongly, rising 1.0% on Monday before giving back some of the gains on Tuesday as DBS, OCBC and UOB came under pressure. The STI then traded around the 5,700 level through the middle of the week before rebounding on Friday.

Friday’s 0.9% gain was supported by renewed buying interest in banks and selected counters, with Yangzijiang Shipbuilding leading the STI components with a 4.66% rise. Hongkong Land gained 3.26% while Singtel advanced 1.80%.

The week’s performance came against a mixed regional backdrop as investors continued to assess global interest-rate expectations, US economic data and regional growth signals.

Market sentiment remained influenced by expectations surrounding US monetary policy, while company earnings and stock-specific developments also kept investors selective.

Despite the mid-week pullback, the STI managed to finish the week above the 5,800 mark, showing resilience as Singapore equities entered September on a firmer footing.

data.title: Plantation Stocks Dominate Bursa’s Top Movers Despite Volatile Week
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia saw a volatile week of trading, with plantation, energy and consumer counters featuring prominently among the market’s biggest daily movers.

Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd emerged as one of the strongest performers across the week, gaining 58 sen on Tuesday and another 41 sen on Wednesday for a combined rise of 99 sen across the two sessions.

Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd was another notable gainer, adding 21 sen on Tuesday and 40 sen on Wednesday, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd gained 86 sen on Wednesday before giving back 32 sen on Thursday.

United Plantations Bhd also featured prominently, climbing 74 sen on Tuesday and 24 sen on Wednesday before suffering a sharp 96 sen decline on Friday.

On the losing side, Nestlé (M) Bhd came under sustained pressure, falling RM2.18 on Tuesday and another RM2.04 on Wednesday. Although it recovered 36 sen on Friday, the counter remained among the week’s biggest decliners based on the reported daily moves.

Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd also saw considerable swings, falling 54 sen on Tuesday and 36 sen on Wednesday before recovering 38 sen on Friday.

Other notable decliners included Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd, which lost RM1.30 on Tuesday and another 48 sen on Wednesday, while Heineken Malaysia Bhd fell 34 sen on Thursday and another 80 sen on Friday.

Friday’s session saw selling pressure return to the market, particularly among plantation stocks, with United Plantations suffering its 96 sen decline.

Meanwhile, selected counters including F&N, Nestlé, CHB, Notion Vtec Bhd and ViTrox Corporation Bhd managed to close higher.

data.title: FBM KLCI Retreats After Merdeka Break As Plantation Stocks Take Hit
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended its shortened trading week lower, with the FBM KLCI falling 17.78 points, or 1.03%, to 1,708.10 on 4 September from 1,725.88 on 29 August.

The market was closed on Monday, 31 August for Merdeka Day, leaving investors with four trading sessions during the week.

The benchmark opened September sharply lower on Tuesday, plunging 25.34 points, or 1.47%, to 1,700.54 as selling pressure intensified across the market. Banks and Tenaga Nasional were among the main drags, while weaker regional markets and geopolitical concerns added to the cautious mood.

Bursa staged a modest recovery on Wednesday, with the FBM KLCI gaining 8.20 points, or 0.48%, to 1,708.74 as bargain-hunting emerged following the previous session’s sell-off.

The index extended its recovery on Thursday, rising to 1,715.13, before giving back 7.03 points, or 0.41%, on Friday.

Friday’s weakness was largely driven by profit-taking in plantation counters following their recent strong run. The FBM Plantation Index fell 156 points as investors locked in gains.

The broader market also remained mixed, with 568 decliners against 523 gainers on Friday. Trading volume stood at 4.33 billion shares worth RM2.98 billion.

For the week, Bursa Malaysia remained under pressure from global risk-off sentiment, geopolitical tensions and concerns over interest-rate expectations. The mid-week rebound offered some relief, but renewed selling in plantation stocks pushed the benchmark back below 1,710 by Friday’s close.

data.title: Kospi Jumps 107.73 Points As Strong Exports, Fed Rate Relief Lift Sentiment
data.description:
South Korean stocks extended gains for a second straight session on Sept 4, with the benchmark Kospi climbing nearly 2% as strong export data and easing concerns over further US interest rate hikes boosted investor appetite.

Yonhap reported that Kospi rose 107.73 points, or 1.64%, to close at 6,687.21, following a 0.26% gain in the previous session. Foreign and institutional investors drove the advance with combined net purchases of 2.15 trillion won, while retail investors sold a net 3.72 trillion won.

Sentiment was supported by comments from US Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller, who signalled he could favour keeping rates unchanged at the Fed’s September meeting as recent data showed signs of easing inflationary pressure.

At home, confidence was strengthened by the Bank of Korea’s latest data showing continued strength in artificial intelligence-related exports. South Korea posted its second-largest current account surplus in July, extending its run of monthly surpluses to 39 consecutive months.

Semiconductor heavyweights led gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 2.2% to 255,500 won and SK hynix advancing 3.2% to 1,647,000 won.

Oil refiners also rallied as heightened US-Iran tensions pushed Brent crude above US$95 a barrel. SK Innovation surged 5.73%, while S-Oil jumped 6.36%. In contrast, LG Energy Solution fell 1.92% and KB Financial declined 3.32%.

Nevertheless, trading remained relatively light, with 235.5 million shares worth 17.46 trillion won changing hands as advancers beat decliners 546 to 309.

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Jump 437.56 Points As Tech, Financials Fuel Broad Rally
data.description:
Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Sept 4, with technology and financial heavyweights driving a broad-based rebound as concerns over an imminent US interest rate hike eased.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index surged 437.56 points, or 1.74%, to 25,650.87, while the Hang Seng Tech Index advanced 2.27% to 4,569.80. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index climbed 2.02% to 8,555.03. Mainboard turnover reached about HK$276.86 billion.

Technology stocks led the charge, rebounding from recent weakness. Lenovo jumped more than 6%, Meituan gained over 5%, Xiaomi rose 3.6%, while Alibaba and Tencent climbed more than 2% each. Xiaomi was additionally supported by news of an agreement with German auto dealers.

Financial counters also strengthened, with China Construction Bank, Agricultural Bank of China and other major mainland lenders advancing, while insurers including China Life posted solid gains. Property shares joined the rally, with Longfor Group surging 8.4% and Sun Hung Kai Properties rising 3.64%.

Sentiment improved after US Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller signalled he was leaning towards keeping interest rates unchanged at the Fed’s September meeting if upcoming inflation data showed further moderation.

The remarks cooled rate-hike fears, eased pressure on global bond markets and helped revive risk appetite across Asian equities.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Rally As Banks, Yangzijiang Lead Gains
data.description:
Singapore shares closed firmly higher on Sept 4, buoyed by gains in the banking heavyweights and Yangzijiang Shipbuilding as easing fears of an imminent US interest rate hike lifted regional sentiment.

The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) climbed 54.25 points, or 0.9%, to 5,801.96, with gainers outnumbering decliners 374 to 210. About 1.3 billion securities worth S$1.9 billion changed hands.

Leading the advance was Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, which jumped 4.7% to S$4.94, supported by its strong earnings performance and the progressive construction of vessels secured at higher contract prices.

Singapore’s three major banks also provided support. DBS rose 0.9% to S$78.65, OCBC gained 1.1% to S$32.27, while UOB added 0.6% to S$42.01. Sembcorp Industries bucked the trend, slipping 1.1% to S$6.11.

The rally came as investors scaled back expectations for a US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike in September, after Fed governor Christopher Waller indicated rates could remain unchanged should inflationary pressures continue to ease. The comments helped cool US Treasury yields and boosted risk appetite across Asian markets ahead of the closely watched US August jobs report.

data.title: Wall Street Slips As Strong Jobs Data Revives Fed Rate Hike Bets
data.description:
Wall Street closed lower on Sept 4 as a stronger-than-expected US jobs report fuelled expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates at its September meeting, triggering a broad sell-off ahead of the Labour Day holiday weekend.

According to Reuters, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 272.51 points, or 0.51%, to 53,413.60, while the S&P 500 declined 0.38% to 7,718.41. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.29% to 26,506.99.

The pressure came after the US economy added 162,000 jobs in August, nearly triple market expectations of 56,000, while June and July payroll figures were revised higher by a combined 55,000. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%.

While the data underscored economic resilience, investors viewed the strong labour market as giving the Fed more room to tighten policy, particularly as higher energy prices linked to geopolitical tensions threaten broader inflationary pressures.

Markets priced in a 58.4% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September, up from 49.4% a day earlier.

Consumer discretionary stocks led losses, while industrials and technology posted modest gains. Semiconductor shares bucked the decline, jumping 3.4%, although the sector remains sharply lower for the quarter.

Among individual stocks, Lululemon Athletica plunged 17.4% after cutting its full-year revenue and profit forecasts, while Adobe dropped 6.7% following news of a leadership transition.

Credit reporting firms also came under heavy pressure, with Fair Isaac tumbling 16.7%, Equifax falling 6.4% and TransUnion dropping 5.9% after moves to expand the use of rival credit-scoring system VantageScore.

Trading volume remained below recent averages as investors headed into the three-day weekend, with US markets closed on Sept 7 for the Labour Day holiday.

data.title: Stock Today: Zetrix AI Rallies 16.67% After RM130 Million MYEG Ventures Clarification
data.description:
Zetrix AI Bhd shares jumped 16.67% to RM0.280 as of 10.44 am, rebounding after trading in the counter was suspended the previous day following a Bursa Malaysia query over its proposed RM130 million acquisition of a 50% stake in MYEG Ventures Inc.

The stock opened at RM0.245 and climbed as high as RM0.290 before easing to RM0.280. It had closed at RM0.240 previously, giving it a gain of RM0.040.

Trading activity was also brisk, with 549.33 million shares changing hands. The counter recorded a low of RM0.245, while the buy price stood at RM0.280 and sell price at RM0.285.

The strong rebound came after Zetrix AI clarified that the acquisition would raise its effective interest in MYEG Philippines Inc to 74.5%, comprising its existing 49% direct stake and a 25.5% indirect interest through MYEG Ventures.

Zetrix AI had earlier incorrectly stated that MYEG Ventures held 60% of MYEG Philippines, before correcting the figure to 51%.

The proposed acquisition involves 15.25 million MYEG Ventures shares, representing the seller’s entire 50% stake. Zetrix AI said the RM130 million consideration would be funded through a combination of new shares and cash.

The company plans to issue up to 360.57 million new ordinary shares, with the issue price to be determined based on the five-day volume-weighted average market price immediately before issuance.

data.title: Asia Markets: Nikkei, KOSPI And Chinese Stocks Climb Ahead Of Payrolls
data.description:
Asian shares climbed on Friday as investors took comfort from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller’s softer stance on interest rates, while markets turned their attention to the latest US jobs data for clues on the Fed’s next move.

Waller said recent data showed signs of disinflation and that he would favour keeping rates steady at this month’s policy meeting if upcoming reports reinforced that trend. Markets subsequently cut the implied probability of a September rate hike to around 50% from about 63% a day earlier.

“Waller is pushing back against the thrust of the argument made by Warsh last week that there is little evidence that underlying inflation has moved lower,” analysts at JPMorgan said in a note.

“We believe that Chair Warsh will deliver a hike if he advocates for it. Absent his advocacy, Governor Waller’s speech reinforces our view that the bar for data to sway the data-dependent majority to hike this month remains elevated.”

The MSCI Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan rose 1%, while Japan’s Nikkei gained 0.8%. Chinese blue-chip stocks climbed 1% and South Korea’s KOSPI advanced 1.1%.

Attention now turns to US nonfarm payrolls, with economists expecting 56,000 jobs to have been added in August after a surprise fall of 23,000 in July. The unemployment rate is expected to remain at 4.1%.

The softer US rate outlook also eased pressure on bonds, with two-year Treasury yields holding at 4.3381% after falling overnight. Ten-year yields stood at 4.7620%.

Meanwhile, the dollar remained under pressure at 98.96 against major currencies, while the yen strengthened to around 155.70 per dollar as traders increased bets on a BOJ rate hike this month.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa In The Red At Midday As Investors Lock In Gains
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia remained lower at midday on Friday as investors took profit following recent gains, with selling pressure particularly evident in industrial products, plantation and financial stocks.

At 12:30pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 8.11 points or 0.47% to 1,707.02 from Thursday’s close of 1,715.13. The index opened 1.39 points lower at 1,713.74.

Market breadth remained negative, with 569 decliners against 419 gainers, while 527 counters were unchanged. Another 1,257 counters were not traded and 19 were suspended.

Trading volume stood at 2.75 billion shares worth RM1.50 billion.

Apex Securities Bhd said the technology sector could remain in focus following Nvidia’s US$12.9 billion AI partnership with Hugging Face, which lifted sentiment across semiconductor-related stocks.

The research house also highlighted the energy sector as Brent crude continued trading above US$95 a barrel amid rising tensions in the Gulf region. Construction stocks could also benefit from continued AI and data centre investments driving demand for related infrastructure and construction works.

Among heavyweights, CIMB Group gained one sen to RM8.00 while Maybank and Tenaga Nasional fell four sen each to RM10.54 and RM13.64 respectively. Public Bank declined two sen to RM4.98 and IHH Healthcare eased one sen to RM7.98.

Zetrix AI was the most actively traded counter, rising 3.5 sen to 27.5 sen, followed by Salutica which gained 4.5 sen to 16 sen.

On the broader market, the FBM ACE Index rose 24.86 points to 5,212.52 while the FBM Emas Index fell 60.64 points to 12,622.70. The Financial Services Index declined 56.84 points and the Plantation Index shed 120.03 points.

data.title: Stock Today: Kerjaya Prospek Gains 3.25% As Data Centre Deal Boosts Sentiment
data.description:
Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd shares rose 3.25% to RM3.18 as of 11.56 am, with the construction counter extending its gains following news of its record RM858 million data centre contract in Johor.

The stock opened at RM3.08 and climbed to an intraday high of RM3.18, while its lowest level was RM3.07. It was up RM0.10 from its previous close of RM3.08.

Trading volume stood at 820,600 shares, with 178 lots on the buy queue at RM3.17 against 480 lots offered at RM3.18.

The latest movement comes after RHB Research maintained its BUY call on Kerjaya Prospek but raised its target price to RM3.87 from RM3.41, implying 34% upside.

The research house said the RM858 million data centre contract, its largest single project to date, represents around 15% of Kerjaya Prospek’s RM5.9 billion outstanding order book.

The contract involves mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works at a data centre in Iskandar Puteri and is expected to start in the third quarter of 2026, with completion targeted within eight months.

The award has brought Kerjaya Prospek’s FY26 contract wins to RM3.2 billion, already above RHB’s previous full-year target of RM2.8 billion. RHB has raised its FY26 job replenishment assumption to RM3.5 billion and sees another RM200 million to RM300 million in potential wins for the remainder of the year.

RHB also raised its earnings forecasts for FY26, FY27 and FY28 by 3%, 6% and 3% respectively, citing stronger contract replenishment and growing exposure to industrial projects including data centres.

data.title: Stock Today: Press Metal Rises 0.75% On Positive Aluminium Outlook
data.description:
Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd shares rose 0.75% to RM8.03 as of 3:58pm on Friday, as investors continued to weigh the group’s outlook against a positive view from RHB Research on the aluminium market.

The counter opened at RM7.90 and climbed to an intraday high of RM8.05 before settling at RM8.03. It had closed at RM7.97 previously, while the day’s low stood at RM7.90.

Trading volume stood at 1.80 million shares, with the stock quoted at RM8.02 on the buy side and RM8.03 on the sell side.

The gain comes after RHB Research maintained its OVERWEIGHT call on the basic materials sector, with Press Metal remaining its top pick as a structural aluminium supply deficit is expected to keep prices elevated.

RHB expects the aluminium market to remain in a deficit of around 900,000 to one million tonnes in 2026, while demand recorded a marginal year-on-year improvement in the first half of the year.

The research house also expects Press Metal to deliver stronger results in 2H26, supported by the lag in aluminium pricing, lower alumina and logistics costs and a higher Main Japanese Ports premium contracted at US$395 per tonne.

RHB maintained its aluminium price assumptions at US$3,250 per tonne for 2026 and US$3,050 for 2027, noting that the year-to-date average of US$3,329 was around 2% above its 2026 assumption.

Longer term, RHB sees Press Metal’s 80%-owned Kalimantan Alumina Nusantara project as a major catalyst, with commissioning scheduled for 2Q27. Once expanded, the project could lift the group’s alumina self-sufficiency to almost 100%, potentially supporting a material improvement in smelting margins.

RHB believes the combination of elevated aluminium prices and structural supply tightness could justify a re-rating of Press Metal above its historical mean.

data.title: Volkswagen Jumps 7% As Historic Restructuring Deal Wins Investor Backing
data.description:
Volkswagen shares jumped 7% in early Frankfurt trading after the automaker reached a major turnaround agreement that eased tensions with unions and shareholder Lower Saxony.

The agreement, approved by Volkswagen’s supervisory board late Thursday, marks the biggest restructuring in the company’s 89-year history and includes a further 50,000 job cuts, bringing total planned reductions across the group to 100,000.

The deal also leaves the future of four German plants undecided, while averting a potential escalation between management, unions and Lower Saxony, which together hold a majority of seats on Volkswagen’s supervisory board.

Management had previously considered calling a shareholder meeting to push through its restructuring demands, which would have marked an unprecedented escalation of the conflict.

“The agreement … is a positive sign for Volkswagen and the capital market – even if it involves severe cutbacks amongst the workforce and within the group,” said Moritz Kronenberger of Volkswagen shareholder Union Investment.

“The ball is now entirely in the Executive Board’s court. There are no more excuses,” he said.

Volkswagen is attempting to improve profitability as it faces pressure from US import tariffs, a stagnant European market and aggressive Chinese competitors.

These pressures have weighed on the group’s operating margin, which stood at just 3.8% in the first half of the year.

Reuters

data.title: F&N Rises 38 Sen To Lead Top Gainers, UtdPlant Falls 96 Sen
data.description:
Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N) led Bursa Malaysia’s top gainers today, rising 38 sen to RM24.76, while United Plantations Bhd (UtdPlant) emerged as the biggest loser, falling 96 sen to RM32.06.

F&N recorded 89,400 shares traded, while Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd followed among the top gainers with a 36 sen increase to RM94.84 on 46,300 shares.

CHB rose 17 sen to RM2.04, with 4.03 million shares changing hands, while Notion Vtec Bhd also gained 17 sen to 68.5 sen on heavy trading volume of 47.70 million shares.

ViTrox Corporation Bhd rounded out the top five gainers, adding 16 sen to RM9.16 with 835,570 shares traded.

On the losing side, UtdPlant fell 96 sen to RM32.06 on 711,700 shares, followed by Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd, which declined 84 sen to RM13.02 with 2.17 million shares traded.

Heineken Malaysia Bhd dropped 80 sen to RM14.84 on 1.15 million shares, while Petronas Gas Bhd fell 36 sen to RM17.26 with 358,500 shares traded.

Hong Leong Bank Bhd completed the top five losers, easing 22 sen to RM23.66 on 182,200 shares.
